advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Escape or validate allow-list paths when interpolating them into the Seatbelt profile (reject/quote special characters).
evidence: scripts/mutation_sandbox.py:82: `lines.append(f'  (subpath "{Path(path).resolve()}")')`
Inputs are `root`, `basetemp`, `Path(sys.prefix)` which are normally safe, but no escaping/validation guards against a path with special characters
advisory.finding: `build_seatbelt_profile` interpolates each allow-list path directly into the Seatbelt profile string with `f'  (subpath "{Path(path).resolve()}")'` without escaping. A path containing a double-quote, newline, or backslash would corrupt the generated profile — either causing sandbox-exec to reject the profile or, worse, silently altering the deny rules. This is a sandbox security control, so a malformed profile that still loads could weaken enforcement.
scenarios: A repo checkout under a directory whose name contains a quote or unusual character; sys.prefix on an unusual venv path

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update docs/mutation-testing.md ('Local use' and/or 'Fresh execution and evidence') to state that mutation_gate.py run now requires an OS sandbox (sandbox-exec or bwrap) and aborts otherwise unless REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED is set.
evidence: scripts/mutation_gate.py:584-603 wraps both subprocesses with mutation_sandbox.wrap(..., allow=sandbox_allow, ...)
scripts/mutation_sandbox.py:120-131 wrap() raises SandboxUnavailable ('refusing to run mutation tests unsandboxed') when probe() returns None and the opt-out is unset

docs/mutation-testing.md:120-126 'Local use' shows `uv run --locked python scripts/mutation_gate.py run ...` with no sandbox precondition; searching docs/mutation-testing.md for 'sandbox' returns no matches
docs/README.md:73 registers docs/mutation-testing.md as the owner: 'Mutation testing workflow and interpretation'
docs/local-dev-env.md:128-151 documents the sandbox requirement, showing the behavior is a documented client/contributor-visible contract but placed only on a different internal page
advisory.finding: docs/mutation-testing.md, the maintained owner of the mutation-testing workflow, still tells contributors to run scripts/mutation_gate.py locally without noting the new sandbox precondition: after this change the baseline pytest and `mutmut run` subprocesses are wrapped by mutation_sandbox.wrap, which aborts the run (SandboxUnavailable) when no OS sandbox (sandbox-exec on macOS, bwrap on Linux) is available unless REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED is set. The 'Local use' commands (and the 'Fresh execution and evidence' contract) omit this requirement, so a contributor on a host without a sandbox mechanism hits an unexplained abort.
scenarios: A contributor follows the mutation-testing.md 'Local use' section on a macOS host without sandbox-exec, or a Linux host without bwrap, and the run aborts with no explanation on that page
advisory.suggested_fix: In docs/mutation-testing.md, add the sandbox precondition to the 'Local use' section (and note it in 'Fresh execution and evidence' alongside the Python 3.12 / mutmut / --max-children contract), e.g. that the run requires bwrap on Linux or sandbox-exec on macOS and aborts without one unless REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED=1 is set, or link to the docs/local-dev-env.md section that describes it.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a construction test for build_seatbelt_profile / the seatbelt wrap() argv (monkeypatch probe()->SEATBELT) asserting the deny-then-allow ordering and subpath entries, mirroring the existing bwrap-argv test.
evidence: scripts/mutation_sandbox.py:73-92 `build_seatbelt_profile` emits `(allow default)`,`(deny file-write*)`,`(allow file-write* (subpath ...))` — order-sensitive Seatbelt semantics

test_mutation_sandbox.py has a bwrap-argv construction test (line 158) but NO seatbelt equivalent: no test asserts build_seatbelt_profile output or that wrap() on SEATBELT returns `["sandbox-exec", "-f", ...]`
The seatbelt branch of wrap() (mutation_sandbox.py:132-136) is reached only when probe()==SEATBELT, i.e. macOS only
advisory.finding: build_seatbelt_profile (added pure function generating the deny-then-allow profile text) has no direct or monkeypatched-construction test analogous to test_bwrap_argv_makes_root_readonly_then_rebinds_allowed. Its only coverage is the macOS-only @live path; on the Linux CI lanes it is never invoked and its output is never asserted, so the profile's deny-all/allow-list ordering contract is unverified anywhere the seatbelt mechanism is absent.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a monkeypatched test that sets sb.shutil.which to return sandbox-exec, calls sb.wrap(...), and asserts argv[:3]==["sandbox-exec","-f",...] and that the written profile contains `(deny file-write*)` before the allow-list subpaths.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace bwrap `--dev-bind /dev /dev` with a minimal `--dev /dev` (fresh devtmpfs) so the Linux sandbox denies raw-device writes, matching the Seatbelt profile's device policy.
evidence: scripts/mutation_sandbox.py:97: `out = ["bwrap", "--ro-bind", "/", "/", "--dev-bind", "/dev", "/dev", "--proc", "/proc"]`
Seatbelt profile only re-permits device writes to specific literals: scripts/mutation_sandbox.py:85-88 `(literal "/dev/null") ... (literal "/dev/stderr") ... (subpath "/dev/fd")`
Module docstring states the sandbox 'denies filesystem writes outside the scratch tree' (docs/local-dev-env.md) yet `--dev-bind` re-binds all of /dev writable, contradicting that on Linux
Enforcement tests (tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py) only assert on regular-file writes (outside.txt, protected/*), never on /dev device nodes, so the bwrap /dev gap is uncovered
advisory.finding: The Linux bwrap sandbox uses `--dev-bind /dev /dev`, bind-mounting the entire real /dev WRITABLE into the sandbox, so a destructive mutant can still write to raw devices (e.g. /dev/sda, /dev/mem) — an unbounded real-host damage path. This is asymmetric with the Seatbelt profile, which only permits writes to /dev/null, /dev/stdout, /dev/stderr, /dev/fd, so the two mechanisms enforce materially different write-deny policies and the bwrap one is a fail-open gap.
scenarios: A mutant on a Linux host reaches a code path that writes to a block device (e.g. `dd of=/dev/sda`), which bwrap permits because /dev is bind-mounted writable, destroying host data despite the sandbox
advisory.suggested_fix: In _bwrap_argv, use `--dev /dev` (bubblewrap's minimal devtmpfs) instead of `--dev-bind /dev /dev`, and add an enforcement test asserting a write to a /dev device node is denied under both mechanisms.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Escape/validate allow-list paths before interpolating them into the Seatbelt profile (reject or quote-escape paths containing `"`, `)`, newlines).
evidence: scripts/mutation_sandbox.py:82: `lines.append(f'  (subpath "{Path(path).resolve()}")')`
Allow paths originate from internal values (root, basetemp, sys.prefix) at scripts/mutation_gate.py:584, so they are not attacker-controlled today
advisory.finding: build_seatbelt_profile interpolates allow-list paths into the Seatbelt profile as double-quoted strings with no escaping; a path containing a `"` or `)` would break the profile syntax and could silently widen or invalidate the write-deny policy.
scenarios: A repo checked out under a path containing a double-quote or paren yields a malformed Seatbelt profile, so sandbox-exec either errors or the deny clause is truncated

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure `basetemp` exists (mkdir parents/exist_ok) before wrapping the baseline pytest argv, since bwrap `--bind` fails on a non-existent source path.
evidence: scripts/mutation_gate.py:566: `basetemp = root / ".mutation-pytest"` — assigned, never mkdir'd
scripts/mutation_gate.py:584: `sandbox_allow = (root, basetemp, Path(sys.prefix))`
scripts/mutation_sandbox.py:100: `out += ["--bind", resolved, resolved]` — bwrap --bind requires the source path to exist
ABSENCE: `search_files` for `.mutation-pytest` returns only the assignment at line 566; nothing creates the directory before wrap() runs
blocking.finding: On Linux, `_bwrap_argv` emits `--bind <resolved> <resolved>` for every allow-list path, but bubblewrap fails if the bind SOURCE does not already exist. `basetemp = root / '.mutation-pytest'` is only assigned (mutation_gate.py:566) and is never created on disk before `mutation_sandbox.wrap(...)` is invoked (mutation_gate.py:587). The baseline pytest run under bwrap will therefore error out ('Can't find source path ...') before pytest can create the basetemp, breaking the mutation gate on Linux hosts.
scenarios: Running the mutation gate on a Linux host with bwrap installed and a fresh checkout where .mutation-pytest has not yet been created
blocking.suggested_fix: Create `basetemp` (e.g. `basetemp.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)`) before calling `mutation_sandbox.wrap`, or have `_bwrap_argv` skip/create non-existent allow paths.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure the bwrap enforcement path is actually exercised in CI (install bubblewrap on the Linux lane so the @live denial tests run, or add a Linux enforcement test), rather than relying on macOS-only seatbelt coverage.
evidence: tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py:38-41 `live = pytest.mark.skipif(sb.probe() is None, reason="no OS sandbox mechanism on this host (sandbox-exec or bwrap)")`
.github search for `bwrap` returned no matches; `bubblewrap` appears only in docs/local-dev-env.md:151 as advice, never in a workflow install step
_mutation.yml:86 `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` with no bwrap install step — the gate's own lane cannot exercise (or even run) the bwrap path

scripts/mutation_sandbox.py:95-103 `_bwrap_argv` produces `--ro-bind / /` + `--bind` rebinds; only tested for shape in test_bwrap_argv_makes_root_readonly_then_rebinds_allowed, never for actual denial
blocking.finding: The bwrap (Linux) enforcement path — actual write-denial — is never exercised in any CI lane. The @live enforcement tests are gated on `pytest.mark.skipif(sb.probe() is None)`, and no workflow installs bwrap/bubblewrap (confirmed: no `apt install bubblewrap` anywhere in .github). On the ubuntu-latest runners where the mutation gate actually runs (_mutation.yml) probe() returns None, so every @live test SKIPS; they run only on macOS cells, exercising the seatbelt path. The mechanism the production gate depends on on Linux thus has only an argv-shape construction test (_bwrap_argv), never a real denial test.
blocking.suggested_fix: Add `sudo apt-get install -y bubblewrap` to the Linux job(s) that run tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py (and to _mutation.yml, since the gate itself aborts without a mechanism), so probe() returns bwrap and the @live denial tests execute on Linux.

evidence: tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py:55-56 `subprocess.run(argv, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)` then `assert not target.exists()` — returncode/stderr captured but never asserted
test_the_incident_shape_rm_rf_is_denied (line 81-82) and test_enforcement_holds_for_the_mutmut_run_argv_shape (line 95-96) follow the same pattern: absence assertion, no producer-liveness anchor
The paired positive test (write_inside_the_allow_list_succeeds, line 60) exists but does not anchor each individual denial test
dropped.finding: Each @live denial test asserts an ABSENCE (`not target.exists()`) after `subprocess.run(..., check=False)` with no liveness check that the sandboxed child actually launched and attempted the write. If sandbox-exec/bwrap fails to spawn the child at all (bad argv, missing /bin/sh, profile parse error), the target is trivially absent and the denial test passes green without the sandbox ever denying anything — a fail-open oracle.
dropped.suggested_fix: In each denial test, have the child also write a marker inside the allow-list (e.g. `echo run > {allowed}/ran && echo pwned > {target}`) and assert the marker exists (child ran) AND target does not (write denied); optionally assert result.returncode is the sandbox-denial code.
